title: Compact prefetch matrix: SDK hydration experiment
body:
Summary:
This is a working PRD sketch for a small, developer-facing experiment: a compact prefetch matrix that drives SDK hydration decisions and graceful tool-proxy fallbacks for the hosted API streaming surface. Goal is to reduce tail latency for common client flows while keeping token cost bounded and making structured-tool outputs more predictable for embedders.

Background / problem:
- Mobile and low-bandwidth clients see long stalls when hosted API calls trigger multiple downstream tool invocations (search, calendar, code-exec).
- Current prefetch heuristics are binary (prewarm vs not) and don’t capture fidelity tradeoffs per-route or per-client profile.
- SDKs have no standard way to hydrate partial session state for resumed streams (reconnect, offline replay).

Hypothesis:
If we expose a compact prefetch policy matrix (latency budget x fidelity tier x tool-residency hints) and use early telemetry signals (first-chunk latency, client bandwidth hint, historical success rate) to pick a hydration plan in the SDK, then median and P95 perceived latency for interactive flows will improve with <=5% increase in token-equivalent cost.

User stories:
- As a mobile product engineer, I want predictable partial-results for tool-backed actions so I can show progressive UI placeholders instead of spinners.
- As an SDK integrator, I want a lightweight API to declare which tool calls are safe to pre-resolve and which must be lazy.
- As platform, I want telemetry hooks that surface prefetch success/failure per-route so we can tune matrix entries without shipping new clients.

Scope / non-goals:
- Do: small experiment across 3 representative routes (reply-assist, doc-summarize+search, code-run snippet). Implement client-side SDK decisions + server-side advisory.
- Do: structured fallback grammar for tool outputs (minimal: COMMIT, PARTIAL, RETRY_HINT).
- Don’t: change core streaming frame format. Don’t redesign tool auth or full offline-first replication.

Design (high-level):
1) Prefetch matrix: server-stored compact table keyed by route tag, fidelity tier (low/medium/high), latency budget (50/150/500ms) and tool affinity flags (resident, cold, optional). Each entry contains a small advisory: prefetch=true/false, max-prefetch-width (how many parallel tool calls), cache-ttl-ms, fallback_strategy.
2) SDK hydration: SDK exposes hydratePlan(routeTag, clientHints) -> plan id + local prefetch orchestration. SDK will attempt pre-resolve for tools marked resident and schedule best-effort prefetch for optional tools.
3) Streaming interplay: streaming frames include optional meta header on first chunk: prefetch-plan-id and structured fallback grammar token to allow partial outputs to be stitched by clients. Servers do not require new frame types; the meta is part of stream-start envelope.
4) Telemetry-first loop: capture prefetch_attempt, prefetch_success, fallback_used, token-cost-estimate per-request. Default sampling 10% for P95 telemetry; route-configurable.

SDK ergonomics:
- New surface: client.prefetchHints({budgetMs: 150, fidelity: "medium", allowBackground: true}) and client.on('partial-tool-output', handler) to receive structured partial envelopes.
- Backwards compatible: if SDK not updated, server falls back to conservative plan (no prefetch).
- Lightweight memory: hydrate plan should fit in <1KB per-route; plan caching TTL default 6 hours.

Structured fallback grammar (initial):
- COMMIT {toolId, payload} -> tool produced final result to stitch in-stream.
- PARTIAL {toolId, summary} -> tool gave partial answer; client may show placeholder and request continuation.
- RETRY_HINT {toolId, reason, suggestedBudgetMs} -> server suggests re-invocation plan.

Experiment plan:
- Stage A (2 weeks): implement matrix config + server advisor endpoint and SDK noop surface that logs decisions. Run on internal beta routes, compare cold vs warmed latency and cost delta.
- Stage B (4 weeks): SDK implements actual prefetch orchestration for resident tools; client UI mock for progressive placeholders. Ramp to 5% traffic.
- Stage C (4 weeks): tighten telemetry loop and run A/B variants of matrix entries to find Pareto points.

Success metrics:
- P50 perceived latency for interactive flows drops by >=20% on targeted routes.
- P95 latency drops by >=10% without >5% token-cost increase.
- Prefetch success rate >70% on resident tools.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Cost blowup if matrix too aggressive -> cap parallel prefetch width and per-request token budget.
- Incorrect client stitching -> start with read-only placeholders and server-side validation for COMMIT frames.
- Observability noise -> include route-tagged sampling and synthetic checkers.

Open questions / notes to resolve:
- How to represent authenticated tool calls in prefetch (proxy token reuse, short-lived credentials)? (security team input needed)
